comment: The class was way too bloated and redundant. The lectures were rehashes of readings we had already done, written reading responses about, and written discussion posts about. There were too many papers, and when we tried to tell him, he kept them, meaning in six papers for the end of the semester, which were redundant and covered the same material.
A lot of essays! Such a sweet teacher

Great professor and guy. Available to meet outside of class/office hours and will review your papers as many times as you send it to him. Nightly homework and quizzes which are stressful, but manageable. Definitely a tough grader which is surprising given his grading philosophy. However, lets you revise 1 essay and notices your effort.

great guy, really is into what he teaches. if you want to get your english gen ed knocked out i highly suggest taking him. offers alot of extra credit and gives a ton of feedback on papers (only write 2 all semester). he really cares about his subject and even more about his students.

Oddly difficult to do well. He gives you essay feedback if you send it to him before the deadlnie, which I did multiple times, but never got higher than a B on those. Class is all lectures and does not reference modern examples, so it can get quite dull sometimes. He is very nice and cares, but I didn't really enjoy the class overall.

Dr. Reckner is a very kind, caring professor. However, lectures are very dull and there are challenging online reading quizzes for every class. There are four essays, two of which count for 30% of your grade each. On essays, he is a fair grader and gives great, thoughtful feedback. Mixed bag overall, don't take if you aren't into philosophy.
Weirdly difficult to get a good grade. One of those classes where your grade is a shot in the dark

Weirdly hard. He grades so few things and class is so informal that for me, I didn't have the opportunity to do as well as I know I could have. After Talking with my friends, it also appears that we all did "OK" but none of us did "great"

Insane. Only graded on three papers and rough drafts of them, and everything is graded based on "genuine effort." So if you at least try to do it, you'll get an A. Never did any of the readings until it was essay time, and he gave you like 6 to choose from. Take if you're looking for an easy A and a blow off class. Good time to do other homework.

Dr. Reckner is a nice guy and a great professor. He has reasonable expectations and does a fantastic job of simplifying difficult philosophical concepts. Students really appreciate that he collects and grades drafts of papers and outlines what to fix for a higher grade.

Dr. Reckner has a somewhat laid-back teaching style. The lectures are clear and at least for the 100 level class I took you were graded well as long as you showed genuine effort, very elaborate or profound writing was not necessary. Lectures were clear and grading expectations were laid out well in the syllabus; mild mannered and agreeable guy.

Class is a few essays, in which he takes your rough drafts and tells you exactly what to do to make them better. Reading and participation is very much optional, as I haven't done anything and am doing just fine in his class. That being said he knows a lot about his subject and can answer any questions you have. Also he has lots of office hours.
